- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is overly optimistic, lower the 30-day mean by 2–5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- After a recent price spike (last 3–5 days), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast slope for next 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” swings (e.g., 1.0 → 0.0 → 1.0), model overfits short-term noise — smooth 30d forecast with 3–5 day moving average.  
- When sentiment is consistently high (e.g., 1.0 for 3+ days), forecast should not exceed 10% above recent 10-day high — cap upward bias.  
- If sentiment is low and price is trending down, model often undercorrects — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- Forecast should not be more than 15% above or below 30-day historical mean unless sentiment is extreme (±0.8).  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is volatile, reduce forecast variance — use 20% smoothing on 30d forecast.
